sources.title: Patan District, Government of Gujarat: History
sources.note: Direct institutional page read for capital identity and named rulers/scholars only. Does not adopt inconsistent city foundation date or page’s reversed Rani-ki-Vav dedication; specialist monument sources used for the well.

sources.title: Masahiko Mita: Charter Forms and Its Implication in Early Medieval India, 2011
sources.note: Original university repository English abstract read in full through indexed result after direct cache failure. Original PDF English abstract printed p. 107 also independently indexed. Analysis distinguishes overlord from subordinate charters; uses document standardization and introduction of document office only.

sources.title: Bhagvanlal Indraji and A. M. T. Jackson: Early History of Gujarat, Bombay Gazetteer I.1, 1896
sources.note: Original government historical study read via full public-domain transcription. Chapter II and III, especially printed pp. 180-194 and 198-203. Bounded uses: Malwa inscription evidence and gradual Vaghela supremacy in 1240s. Later Jain legends, royal character judgments, and exact disputed reign endpoints not adopted.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Rani-ki-Vav, Patan
sources.note: Direct full OUV and integrity text read: eleventh-century memorial and water architecture, seven levels, sculptures, thirteen-century silting, groundwater/river changes and preservation. Exact contradictory dimensions from other sites not mixed.

sources.title: Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts: Rani-ki-Vav, Patan
sources.note: Direct original institutional description read: construction attributed to Udayamati, wife of Bhimadeva I. Attribution retained as such; does not invent a contemporary foundation inscription.

sources.title: Permanent Delegation of India to UNESCO: Sun Temple, Modhera, tentative-list submission
sources.note: Full 2022 submission read: eleven-century dating by style in Bhima I reign; shrine, assembly hall, tank, Surya imagery, carved musicians/animals and narrative ceilings. Tentative nomination is not World Heritage inscription; equinox alignment and legendary foundation omitted.

sources.title: Patan District: Sahastra Ling Talav
sources.note: Direct indexed original government description read: earlier Durlabh reservoir renewed under Siddharaj, royal and citizen water patronage. Avoid exact construction date and unverified curse legends.

sources.title: Bhavnagar Archaeological Department: Collection of Prakrit and Sanskrit Inscriptions, Mangrol record, pp. 158-160
sources.note: Primary edition read in direct full-text mirror: reader pages 235 and 238-239, printed pp. 158-160, Gohila dynasty I. Sanskrit transcription and English translation. Mangrol stone reused in stepwell wall, temple family dedication, grain/pack-animal/betel revenues and donated well. Dated VS 1202; introductory CE conversion says 1146 while modern catalogues give 1145, so public uses mid-1140s/VS 1202. OCR flawed elsewhere; short नमः शिवाय is legible in transcription and translated Salutation to Siva.

sources.title: Ranabir Chakravarti: Merchants, Merchandise and Merchantmen in the Western Seaboard of India, 2012
sources.note: Original scholarly chapter read through PDF mirror, especially printed p. 83 (PDF index 32): Chaulukya regional power, agricultural hinterland, intermediary markets, Cambay and twelfth-century Diu letter. Broad later Indian Ocean evidence not backdated.

sources.title: Pushpa Prasad: Lekhapaddhati, Documents of State and Everyday Life from Ancient and Medieval Gujarat, 2007
sources.note: Publisher’s original abstract read directly, not full subscription book: actual/model documents spanning centuries, scribes, credit/mortgages, private letters and enslaved girls. Collection has a long transmission history; card does not treat every form as an event in 1100-1200.

sources.title: Cleveland Museum of Art: Hemachandra Dvyashraya manuscript folio, 1971.131
sources.note: Direct object record and print version read. Object is 1428, Gujarat possibly Patan; text composed 1160; grammar and praised royal deeds. Later illustration identifies Hemachandra and Kumarapala and depicts ascetic cloth/broom. Clearly distinguished from a contemporary portrait. Museum supplies dynasty 940-1244 and Kumarapala 1143-1172.

proposedOverrides.name: Solankis of Gujarat
proposedOverrides.summary: A western Indian kingdom centered on Patan, with influential water architecture, royal scholarship and connected markets.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Exact missing record only. Gujarat Chaulukyas/Solankis distinguished from already covered Badami and Kalyani Chalukyas and much later Gujarat Sultanate. No aliases.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Decoded world-1100 multipolygon, properties 1100-1200, bbox [68.07128071280712,20.65086144789501,76.92016920169203,25.713483747854596]. Broad western Indian outline simplifies shifting conquest, suzerainty and local government; public warning included.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Map 1100-1200 maintained. Earlier monuments dated as eleventh-century context; political transition in 1240s separated from map endpoint. Royal reign years vary slightly across older studies, so period boundaries are circa and most public prose uses broad phases. Cleveland 1428 manuscript copy explicitly later.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Primary Mangrol inscription edition, Gohila I, pp.158-160. VS1202, mid-1140s; sample is namah sivaya only, clear Devanagari transcription and corresponding English translation. Regional subordinate/local donor evidence in Kumarapala reign, not royal autograph.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: Local monuments and a specific customs/temple endowment are not universal household practices. No excavated domestic toilet or medical treatment identified in selected evidence, so no invented sanitation/medicine claims. Water supply, family memorials and unequal households provide grounded daily-life coverage.
